overview: Rapid review of pharmacist-led follow-up for adults starting oral anticancer agents, following rapid review methods guidance, with three strands reported separately: harms and dose intensity, adherence by measurement method, and pharmacist time and money. No figure combines strands.
population: Studies and reports of adults starting oral anticancer agents (any tumour type) receiving pharmacist-led follow-up, 2010 onward, English only, including cancer centre and health technology assessment agency reports.
exposure: Pharmacist-led follow-up in the first weeks of oral treatment: consultation before the first cycle, telephone toxicity and adherence checks, review before supplies, alone or combined.
procedures: The library searches three bibliographic databases and agency websites. One pharmacist screens all titles and abstracts; the second screens a 20 percent random sample and all excluded full texts. Extraction uses one form with a strand field; key outcomes are verified by the second pharmacist. Risk of bias is judged for trials and comparative studies only, at the level the time allows. The search hits reported but not returned by the first search are retrieved before screening closes.

outcomes.name: Unplanned toxicity admissions and severe toxicity
outcomes.measure: Proportion admitted for toxicity or with grade 3 or worse toxicity within 90 days, as reported
outcomes.why: Patient-important, and the basis of any saving.

outcomes.name: Service cost and admission costs averted
outcomes.measure: Annual service cost and reported averted admission costs, each as a range with its assumptions, never netted into a single figure
outcomes.why: The committee's funding question, kept separate from effects.

outcomes.name: Adherence by measurement method
outcomes.measure: Adherence as reported, tabulated separately for pill count, refill data, electronic caps and self-report
outcomes.why: Measures disagree by up to 12 points (claim c2).

outcomes.name: Relative dose intensity
outcomes.measure: Relative dose intensity over the first three cycles, or as reported
outcomes.why: Earlier dose reductions may trade toxicity for less treatment (claim c4).

outcomes.name: Pharmacist time per patient
outcomes.measure: Pharmacist hours per patient over the first 12 weeks
outcomes.why: Sets the staffing the service needs (claim c6).

outcomes.name: Patients' views of pharmacist follow-up
outcomes.measure: Reported acceptability, reasons for calls being welcome or intrusive, and who was not reached
outcomes.why: Acceptability, and who the service may miss (claim c7).

feasibility: About 144 pharmacist hours to 29 January 2027; searches confirmed; the remaining hits add an estimated 5 hours of screening.
biasMitigation: Adherence never pooled across measurement methods
Costs reported as ranges with assumptions
Population age, living situation, distance and language charted for every study

biasFlags.label: Single screening
biasFlags.note: A 20 percent sample and all excluded full texts are checked by the second pharmacist.

biasFlags.label: Incomplete retrieval
biasFlags.note: Eleven reported hits were not returned by the first search; the gate stays unknown until they are retrieved.

flags: Cost outcome recorded as secondary with its own strand; dose intensity as balancing; time as process
parsimony.simplestPath: Three strands, one extraction form, no combined figure.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond rapid review methods; strands follow the committee's request.
summary: Corrected protocol: one primary harm outcome, cost and adherence as separate secondary strands, dose intensity as balancing and pharmacist time as process.
